protocol.scope: Independent adversarial novelty and reviewer critique of exactly O1, O2 and O3 from the supplied literature.json. No overall GO assessment.
protocol.blinding: The original blind audit was preserved unchanged. No benchmark or benchmark-key files were inspected. Candidate descriptions and their cited primary-source text caches were read only after the explicit candidate-audit request.
protocol.method: Read the actual cached primary text behind the closest threats, distinguish implemented mechanisms from future-work statements, and test each proposed distinction with counterexamples and evaluation requirements. No experiments were authorized or executed.
limitations: The original follow-up phase independently inspected shared cached primary-source text. A subsequently authorized six-request phase independently searched and retrieved three additional papers; its evidence and costs are separated below.
The later searches are bounded and non-exhaustive. In particular, only 50 of 170 returned O3 results were screened, with substantial lexical noise. Missing search hits cannot establish novelty.
No dataset release, license, annotation package or implementation was downloaded or tested.
Primary-text snapshots are retained with verified hashes. Hashes are for extracted text, not original PDFs.
Source statements are evidence of what authors report, not independent reproduction.
The conclusions concern the submitted candidate descriptions. They do not prove that every possible narrower implementation is unoriginal.

new_decisive_findings.finding: RIC-Loc already reports full-set behavior, including ineligible queries. All-query evaluation is therefore not a sufficient novelty distinction.
new_decisive_findings.required_correction: Replace the contrast with covariance-eligible subsets by the actual distinction: UAV map-footprint dependence under geographic shift, compared against RIC-Loc's existing full-set/fallback accounting.

new_decisive_findings.finding: RIC-Loc does more than ignore all shared uncertainty: its covariance adds a common-mode scale term and residual-consistency inflation. It still explicitly acknowledges unmodeled inter-hypothesis dependence.
new_decisive_findings.required_correction: Do not frame the baseline as wholly dependence-blind. Isolate remaining cross-hypothesis correlation from the already implemented common-mode treatment.

new_decisive_findings.finding: SkyReg already predicts per-pixel confidence and trains with a confidence-weighted regression objective.
new_decisive_findings.required_correction: Make SkyReg/MASt3R point confidence an explicit strong baseline when outputs are available. Generic pixel confidence or withholding uncertain pixels is not an adequate contribution.

new_decisive_findings.finding: OrthoLoC explicitly supplies point maps, local meshes, camera calibration and pose; it is not merely an image-level pose-truth source. However, its same-domain geodata and geometry truth share a reconstruction source.
new_decisive_findings.required_correction: Separate documented annotation types from unverified release accessibility. Use cross-domain geodata for map-error claims and account for reconstruction/georeferencing dependence.

new_decisive_findings.finding: HF-Net's hierarchy already clusters prior frames by co-observed 3D structure. RIC-Loc explicitly proposes selecting references by viewpoint diversity, predicted track support and conditioning rather than fixed top-K.
new_decisive_findings.required_correction: Strengthen overlap beyond generic hierarchical retrieval. Show a difference from covisibility grouping and articulated geometry-aware selection, not just from descriptor top-K.

candidates.title: Geographic dependence-aware abstention for retrieved UAV pose hypotheses
candidates.reviewer_position: Reject generic confidence-fusion, consensus, abstention and all-query-evaluation novelty claims. Retain only a narrowly falsifiable dependence-diagnostic question, without declaring it novel.
observed_prior_art: RIC-Loc implements reference-induced hypotheses, robust consensus, dispersion/covariance failure ranking, held-out selection and risk-coverage; it also reports full-set behavior.
RIC-Loc already includes common-mode scale uncertainty and residual-consistency inflation, while explicitly acknowledging remaining correlation and limited eligibility.

RIM explicitly proposes calibrated fusion of retrieval margins, correspondence support/coverage, geometric statistics, PnP residuals and temporal consistency. This is future work, not an implemented calibrated RIM rejector.

strongest_counterexample.status: inferred counterexample, not an observed experimental result
strongest_counterexample.description: All retrieved tiles may support the same wrong but internally consistent building alias. Leaving out one overlapping footprint cluster can leave essentially the same wrong pose. A low leave-one-cluster-out displacement does not certify correctness. Conversely, spatially diverse tiles may still share the same matcher, map bias or repeated architecture.
strongest_counterexample.implication: Footprint diversity is neither necessary nor sufficient for independent pose errors. Demonstrate that it predicts additional held-out error beyond ordinary hypothesis spread and support counts.

missing_method_specification: Define overlap, clustering and linkage. Connected components of an overlap graph can merge a long tile chain into one cluster even when endpoints barely overlap.
With top_k=5, specify behavior for one cluster, singleton clusters, no pose, no surviving hypotheses and a leave-one-cluster-out refit failure. These cannot be silently removed from evaluation.
Define whether the score changes the estimator or only rejects its fixed output. Freeze the estimator across confidence baselines to prevent accuracy changes from masquerading as better uncertainty.
Specify whether cached pose hypotheses already share features, reference content or map geometry; geographic overlap is only one possible source of dependence.
minimum_falsification_experiment: Run matched-candidate, matched-estimator comparisons: complete confidence fusion; fusion plus effective footprint count; fusion plus the proposed leave-one-cluster-out statistic. Match model capacity and tuning budget.

Distinguish same-geography duplicate support, genuinely different valid support, systematic map bias, and a consistent wrong-place consensus. Deliberate duplication/removal is a diagnostic stress test, not the main deployment distribution.
Report the number of independent test sites and flights, not just 400 queries. Use site/flight-grouped uncertainty and predeclare one primary failure threshold.
Count solver failures and undefined scores as failures/ineligible cases in all-query accounting. State their rank policy and maximum attainable acceptance coverage.
At a fixed calibration-selected threshold, report empirical held-out risk and coverage. Do not equate an empirical 10% calibration target with a geographic-shift guarantee.

A merely nonnegative bootstrap improvement interval is too ambiguous: define the interval level and whether its lower bound must exceed zero, while separating screening thresholds from scientific significance.
candidates.surviving_claim_if_supported: A specific, reproducible footprint-dependence statistic adds predictive value over strong shared-error and confidence-fusion baselines for a clearly defined UAV map-reference setting.
candidates.stop_rule: Drop the method claim if footprint count alone explains the result, if the gain disappears against full fusion/common-mode baselines, or if unsupported/undefined cases are required to disappear from the denominator.
candidates.uncertainty: The exact footprint statistic may have a useful narrow role. Neither novelty against classical correlated estimators nor a real-world gain is established.

candidates.title: Geometry-sensitivity gating for off-nadir pixel-to-map anchors
candidates.reviewer_position: The diagnostic could be useful, but finite-difference geometry sensitivity plus thresholding is not yet a distinct method. The most serious threat is standard error propagation, compounded by existing dense point confidence.
observed_prior_art: SkyReg implements dense point maps and confidence-weighted regression with per-pixel confidences, so a confidence baseline is already available in the method.
SkyReg's benchmark is not uniformly real UAV data: its dataset section describes Google Earth-rendered drone imagery and differing sources of depth geometry.
OrthoLoC provides real UAV queries, reconstructed point maps/meshes, and same-domain plus external cross-domain DOP/DSM. Its pairing is ground-truth-assisted to isolate localization from retrieval.
OrthoLoC already examines covisibility and geometry/calibration limitations; improved sensitivity plots alone are not a new task.

strongest_counterexample.status: auditor mathematical reasoning, not a cited new result
strongest_counterexample.description: For a fixed camera ray x(t)=o+t*d intersecting a horizontal plane of height h, the horizontal derivative with respect to h is (d_x/d_z,d_y/d_z); its norm is tan(off-nadir angle). A constant-height finite-difference score can therefore reduce to a simple viewing-angle score rather than a novel learned or geometric diagnostic.
strongest_counterexample.implication: Compare against analytic ray/height sensitivity and propagated pose/height covariance, not only residuals and inlier confidence. For nonplanar terrain, test what additional information is supplied beyond local slope, incidence angle and known elevation uncertainty.

missing_method_specification: The question mentions camera perturbations, but the stated experiment specifies only height offsets. Define intrinsic/extrinsic perturbations, parameter units, correlation, and how magnitudes are obtained without ground truth.
Distinguish global elevation bias, spatially varying elevation noise, local relief/slope errors and outright wrong-surface correspondence. A uniform 1/3/5 m shift does not test all of them.
Holding matches fixed isolates propagation conditional on the matches; it cannot establish a full system's robustness when geometric changes alter correspondences, visibility or solver convergence.

Homography and PnP require comparable output coordinates and visibility conventions. Disagreement can be caused by planar-model mismatch, solver instability or wrong matches; it is not itself a calibrated probability.
Specify horizontal geodetic error versus vertical error and 3D Euclidean error. Haversine distance alone cannot validate elevation accuracy.
Keep same-reconstruction and external-geodata tests separate. Do not synthesize truth by intersecting the same perturbed DSM used by the predictor.

OrthoLoC transforms geometric elements into local coordinates for privacy; local metric evaluation is possible, but a global latitude/longitude claim requires verifying that the necessary frame transform is actually released.
minimum_falsification_experiment: First verify released point maps, validity masks, camera data and independent cross-domain DSM access. The paper documents these modalities; actual download access remains unverified.

Use residual plus match confidence, SkyReg/MASt3R point confidence where applicable, off-nadir/local-slope covariates, analytic ray sensitivity and first-order covariance propagation as explicit baselines.

Evaluate score ranking on fixed original valid anchors. Report within-query equal-coverage results as well as pooled coverage so discarding difficult images cannot masquerade as better individual-anchor selection.
Use external DSM versus the original reconstruction-derived point truth for a separately identified real map-error test, with georeferencing/reconstruction noise acknowledged.
Test where the model is confidently wrong, not only where its assumptions predict large variance. Systematic map shifts or wrong repeated structures may have low local sensitivity.
Predeclare the primary error threshold, coverage, perturbation family and held-out geography. Pixel counts do not supply independent sample size; bootstrap sites/queries.
If only CPU classical matches are available, restrict conclusions to a sensitivity mechanism screen. Do not claim superiority to dense learned systems that were not run.
candidates.surviving_claim_if_supported: A defined diagnostic captures a failure mode not explained by conventional propagated uncertainty, viewing geometry or existing point confidence, and improves selective metric accuracy against independent map-error truth.
candidates.stop_rule: Drop method novelty if analytic sensitivity or basic angle/slope features match the result; block geodetic claims if truth shares the evaluated map errors or the required coordinate/visibility data are unavailable.
candidates.uncertainty: The classical prior-art search is still incomplete. Existing evidence supports a significant novelty threat, not a definitive bibliographic proof that the exact proposed score has already appeared.

candidates.title: Fixed-budget candidate selection by independent geometric support
candidates.novelty_assessment: uncertain; high-level selection principle explicitly anticipated
candidates.reviewer_position: Maintain hold. Reject novelty of generic diversity, support-based selection, hierarchical localization or geometry-aware reranking. A fixed budget is an evaluation constraint, not by itself a new selection principle.
observed_prior_art: RIC-Loc explicitly proposes viewpoint-diverse, track-supported, well-conditioned reference selection instead of fixed top-K. This is a direct conceptual anticipation, not evidence that the paper implemented and evaluated the proposed selector.
HF-Net already groups retrieved references by co-observed 3D structure before geometric localization.
UnifyGeo implements a learned reranking mechanism connecting retrieval and metric localization. Training-free operation is a deployment distinction, not automatic novelty.

strongest_counterexample.status: inferred counterexample, not an observed benchmark result
strongest_counterexample.description: If only one small region is correct, forcing geographic diversity can spend the budget on irrelevant regions and remove useful redundant views of the correct place. Conversely, repeated observations of a correct structure can improve robustness rather than represent wasted evidence.
strongest_counterexample.implication: Useful diversity must be conditioned on correctness and observability. Demonstrate marginal geometric utility, not merely lower overlap or a larger geographic spread.

missing_method_specification: Define what new spatial support means before an expensive match is available, how support from different references is put in a shared frame, and how uncertain cheap correspondences are discounted.
Do not call a score-plus-diversity greedy rule independent geometric support without evidence that it models dependence or predicts marginal pose information.
Specify the baseline candidate pool, reference resolution and feature-cache policy. Geographic NMS and covisibility grouping should receive the same information as the proposed selector.
State whether cached learned outputs were generated for all top-20 pairs. That expense cannot disappear from a claim of online fixed-budget efficiency.
minimum_falsification_experiment: Use a real non-oracle gallery and fixed top-20 candidate pool. OrthoLoC's paired reference crop alone cannot establish global candidate-selection gains.
Compare score-only, geographic NMS, covisibility/support grouping, simple diversity selection, support-only and combined policies with frozen localization backends.
Report fixed expensive-pair-count results and separate equal end-to-end resource results. Two full matches plus twenty cheap probes is not equivalent to two full matches without probes.
Charge probe decoding, descriptors, matching, CPU/GPU transfer, geometric solves and reference preprocessing/storage. Distinguish reusable offline map work from per-query work.

Report both candidate-available conditional diagnostics and all-query metric success, including no-pose failures. Show whether gains come from improved candidate recall or improved geometric conditioning.
Test multiple geographic regions and query geometries. A 5-point success gain over descriptor top-K is insufficient if NMS or covisibility grouping produces the same gain.
A bounded CPU ORB fallback can diagnose redundancy but cannot by itself falsify or validate the learned pipeline under its intended feature errors.
candidates.surviving_claim_if_supported: A precisely specified pre-match utility estimator has a demonstrable advantage over standard diversity/covisibility baselines under a complete online resource ledger.
candidates.stop_rule: Drop if a simple grouping/NMS baseline matches it, if the selection probes erase the resource advantage, or if gains require oracle reference crops or uncharged cached pair matches.
candidates.uncertainty: Active localization and optimal-design literature were not exhaustively examined. The candidate's broad principle is already anticipated, while novelty of an unspecified narrower rule cannot be established or definitively rejected.

followup_costs.accounting: Original shared-cache critique: zero HTTP requests. Additional independent candidate search: six requests, as separately itemized below. Original blind-audit costs remain in blind-audit.json and are not included here.

independent_search.status: bounded search completed; candidate novelty remains unresolved
independent_search.research_boundary: All three searches and full-paper inspections were completed before reading overlap-results, seed-source-verification, runtime-smoke-observations, operator-verification-log or validation implementation for the report. No benchmark key was read.
independent_search.provenance_distinction: These are new public search responses and primary PDFs obtained directly by the independent auditor, not copied from the literature investigator. The original shared-cache analysis above remains a separate evidence phase.
independent_search.raw_evidence: Exact returned search HTML, all three original PDF response bodies and extracted text are retained. The retrieval log maps URLs to filenames and SHA-256 values for every response and PDF text extraction.
independent_search.request_policy: One search and one full-paper request per candidate; six total HTTP GET requests; redirects disabled; no retry or further search.

searches.selection_reason: Directly addresses multiple sources of partially known correlation; more mechanistically relevant to dependence-aware fusion than an unrelated generic confidence paper.

other_retained_lead.access_level: abstract in retained search response only
other_retained_lead.observed: The 2016 abstract applies covariance intersection to priors that might become correlated. Its full paper was not fetched and no detailed theorem claim is made.

searches.selection_reason: Direct UAV/aerial per-point uncertainty propagation paper covering camera and stereo errors and anchor-point cross-covariance.
A primary optimal-design formulation for fixed-budget geometric sensor subset selection, stronger as a mechanism threat than generic coverage optimization.

primary_findings.title: Overlapping Covariance Intersection: Fusion with Partial Structural Knowledge of Correlation from Multiple Sources
primary_findings.evidence_location: Section I.B, PDF page 3, CI variants; Section II, PDF page 4, Equation 4 and linear fusion formulation.
primary_findings.quote: linear fusion law that provides an unbiased estimator
primary_findings.observed: OCI explicitly models partially known correlation from multiple information sources and optimizes a conservative linear fusion construction. Its formulation assumes known linear measurement matrices, zero-mean errors and structured covariance information.
primary_findings.mechanism_threat: Treating overlapping evidence sources as correlated and using partial dependence information is not a new principle. O1 needs a particular usable diagnostic beyond existing correlated-estimate treatments.
primary_findings.non_equivalence: Map-footprint overlap does not automatically supply OCI's covariance bounds or zero-mean assumptions. A common wrong-building alias is a biased error, and this paper does not establish UAV abstention performance. The O1 leave-one-footprint-out statistic is not proven identical to OCI.
primary_findings.verdict_update: Stronger independently retrieved prior-art threat; O1 remains uncertain, not established novel or conclusively identical.

primary_findings.title: Uncertainty Quantification Framework for Aerial and UAV Photogrammetry through Error Propagation
primary_findings.inspected_version: Current PDF fetched; search response reports revised submission 29 April 2026. No arXiv version marker was found in the extracted PDF text; do not infer a version number.
primary_findings.evidence_location: Section 2.3, PDF page 5; Figure 2 and uncertainty propagation/anchor covariance, PDF page 6, Equations 1–2.
primary_findings.quote: The uncertainty propagated from SfM captures the low-frequency, systematic errors that affect the entire model
primary_findings.observed: The paper propagates camera/SfM and disparity/MVS uncertainty into per-point covariance, differentiates model-wide from local geometric errors, and describes full covariance including cross-covariances for sparsely sampled anchor points.
primary_findings.mechanism_threat: Per-anchor uncertainty obtained from camera/measurement error propagation has direct prior art. A perturbation score must be compared against analytic/full-covariance propagation, not merely image residuals.
primary_findings.non_equivalence: Its task reconstructs photogrammetric point clouds, not selective drone-to-map anchor validity under erroneous external DSMs. It does not by itself establish the proposed abstention policy or its claimed geodetic gains.
primary_findings.verdict_update: O2's generic uncertainty-propagation claim is substantially weakened. A distinct external-map-error diagnostic remains unresolved and untested.

primary_findings.title: OASIS: Optimal Arrangements for Sensing in SLAM
primary_findings.evidence_location: Abstract and Figure 1, PDF page 1; Sections II and III.B, PDF pages 2–3.
primary_findings.quote: We assume that each of these is sampled independently from a known sensor model
primary_findings.observed: OASIS formulates sensor arrangement as budgeted subset selection under an E-optimal Fisher-information objective, using greedy selection and convex-relaxation verification. It explicitly assumes independent measurements and recognizable landmarks.
primary_findings.mechanism_threat: Selecting a fixed number of geometric information sources by conditioning/information utility is established optimal-design practice, rather than a new principle supplied by a matching budget.
primary_findings.non_equivalence: Selecting physical sensor mountings is not selecting satellite reference images with uncertain associations. The independence and known-model assumptions do not automatically hold for O3. No exact retrieved-reference selector was established by this bounded search.
primary_findings.verdict_update: Maintain hold. Broad conditioning-aware fixed-budget selection is not defensible novelty; a particular pre-match utility model would need a narrower distinction and empirical evidence.

failures_and_limits: All six requests returned HTTP 200; no network retries or paid services were used.
ArXiv lexical search was noisy: O1 included an unrelated covariant-membrane paper, and O3 included many unrelated astronomy, re-identification and visualization papers. These were excluded.
O3 screening covered only the first 50 of 170 matches, ordered by announcement date; the remaining 120 were not retrieved.
One PDF extraction emitted a font-type mismatch warning; extraction completed. Exact PDFs are retained, so text extraction is not the sole evidence artifact.
These are targeted threats, not a systematic classical-literature review. Historical foundational references mentioned inside the papers were not separately fetched.
The new PDFs and search pages are contemporary retrievals. They do not establish a model-blinded historical novelty assessment or leakage-free retrospective.
Partial search remains uncertainty. No candidate was promoted to novel because a more exact match was not found.

costs.elapsed_scope: Wall time from first independent search request through evidence/accounting freeze; excludes subsequent JSON/report composition.
